stem: A 55-year-old man with resistant hypertension did well on spironolactone but has painful breast enlargement. Potassium is normal. Which change keeps the benefit and addresses the complaint?
correct: Switch to eplerenone

distractors.text: Switch to amiloride plus a potassium supplement
distractors.why: Supplements add hyperkalemia risk with potassium-sparing drugs.

distractors.text: Switch to triamterene and add trimethoprim
distractors.why: Trimethoprim adds hyperkalemia risk.

distractors.text: Continue spironolactone and add finasteride
distractors.why: That does not address the antiandrogen effect.

distractors.text: Switch to acetazolamide for the same receptor effect
distractors.why: It acts in the proximal tubule, not at the aldosterone receptor.

why_correct: Spironolactone has antiandrogen effects (gynecomastia, menstrual irregularities) that eplerenone largely avoids. Both block the aldosterone receptor.
takeaway: Gynecomastia on spironolactone: eplerenone.
discriminator: Same receptor, fewer antiandrogen effects.

stem: A 66-year-old on metoprolol after a myocardial infarction needs a calcium channel blocker for blood pressure. Which choice avoids a conduction problem, and what should she be told to expect?

distractors.text: Verapamil; constipation can occur
distractors.why: Verapamil with a beta-blocker risks bradycardia and AV block.

distractors.text: Diltiazem; ankle swelling can occur
distractors.why: Diltiazem with a beta-blocker carries the same conduction risk.

distractors.text: Amlodipine; a slow pulse can occur
distractors.why: Dihydropyridines cause reflex tachycardia, not bradycardia.

distractors.text: Verapamil; reflex tachycardia can occur
distractors.why: Verapamil slows the heart.

why_correct: Diltiazem or verapamil with a beta-blocker risks bradycardia and AV block; dihydropyridines pair with beta-blockers without that risk. Dihydropyridines cause peripheral edema and reflex tachycardia.
takeaway: With a beta-blocker, choose a dihydropyridine.
discriminator: Vessel-selective vs heart-slowing CCBs.

stem: A 74-year-old takes losartan and furosemide. After a week of over-the-counter ibuprofen for knee pain, creatinine has doubled. Which explanation is most complete?
correct: Afferent constriction, efferent dilation and volume loss together

distractors.text: Ibuprofen alone is directly toxic to the renal tubules
distractors.why: The lecture's point is the three combined hemodynamic hits.

distractors.text: Losartan caused bradykinin build-up in the glomerulus
distractors.why: ARBs do not act through bradykinin.

distractors.text: Furosemide caused hyperkalemia that injured the kidney
distractors.why: Loops lower potassium.

distractors.text: Efferent constriction from ibuprofen raised filtration
distractors.why: NSAIDs constrict the afferent arteriole and filtration falls.

why_correct: NSAID (afferent constriction) + ACE inhibitor or ARB (efferent dilation) + diuretic (volume depletion): filtration pressure collapses. Common, often missed and preventable; ask about OTC NSAIDs.
takeaway: ACEi/ARB + diuretic + NSAID = AKI.
discriminator: Each drug alone is tolerated; the three together are not.

stem: A 64-year-old with stable angina took sildenafil last evening. He now has chest pain and reaches for his sublingual nitroglycerin. Why is this dangerous?

distractors.text: Sildenafil blocks nitrate absorption under the tongue
distractors.why: The interaction is additive vasodilation.

distractors.text: Both cause reflex bradycardia and AV block
distractors.why: That is the verapamil or diltiazem with beta-blocker risk.

distractors.text: Sildenafil causes nitrate tolerance within hours
distractors.why: Tolerance comes from continuous nitrate exposure.

distractors.text: Both constrict the afferent arteriole: kidney injury
distractors.why: That is the NSAID mechanism.

why_correct: Nitrates donate NO and raise cGMP; PDE5 inhibitors block cGMP breakdown. Together they cause life-threatening hypotension.
takeaway: Nitrate + PDE5 inhibitor: never.
discriminator: Make more cGMP + stop its breakdown.

distractors.why: More continuous exposure deepens tolerance.

distractors.text: Add sildenafil to boost the nitrate's cGMP signal

distractors.why: Rebound hypertension is the clonidine issue.

stem: An 84-year-old with CKD is admitted with a serious infection and needs a renally cleared antibiotic. Her creatinine clearance is markedly reduced. Which dosing approach matches the lecture?
correct: Usual loading dose, then a reduced maintenance dose

distractors.text: Reduced loading dose, then the usual maintenance dose
distractors.why: Loading is often unchanged; maintenance is what is adjusted.

distractors.text: Usual loading and usual maintenance, with levels if toxic
distractors.why: A renally cleared drug accumulates when GFR is low.

distractors.text: No loading dose, then double the interval and the dose
distractors.why: Skipping the load delays effect; doubling the dose defeats the cut.

discriminator: Loading fills the volume; maintenance replaces what is cleared.

stem: A 70-year-old with CKD (GFR 24) has worsening leg edema and blood pressure 162/94 on hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, lisinopril and amlodipine. He takes all three reliably. Which change is most likely to help?

stem: A 63-year-old with decompensated heart failure and pulmonary edema has a head injury with raised intracranial pressure. A resident suggests mannitol. What is the main concern?
correct: Mannitol expands extracellular volume and can worsen overload

distractors.text: Mannitol causes metabolic acidosis and potassium loss
distractors.why: That is acetazolamide.

distractors.text: Mannitol causes hyperkalemia with ACE inhibitors
distractors.why: That is the potassium-sparing class.

distractors.text: Mannitol loses efficacy once GFR is below about 30
distractors.why: That is the thiazide cutoff.

distractors.text: Mannitol causes gynecomastia through antiandrogen action
distractors.why: That is spironolactone.

why_correct: Mannitol is used for raised intracranial or intraocular pressure, but it expands extracellular volume: avoid it in heart failure and volume depletion. Monitor osmolality and electrolytes.
takeaway: Mannitol: right for ICP, wrong for a failing heart.
discriminator: It pulls water into the vessels before it leaves.

stem: A 67-year-old with heart failure takes digoxin and has had furosemide increased twice this month. She now has nausea, visual changes and new ectopy. Potassium is 3.0 mEq/L. Which statement explains this?
correct: Loop-induced hypokalemia has increased digoxin toxicity

distractors.text: Furosemide has raised digoxin levels by blocking CYP3A4
distractors.why: The taught link is through potassium, not CYP.

distractors.text: Loop-induced hyperkalemia has blocked digoxin's effect
distractors.why: Loops lower potassium.

distractors.text: Furosemide ototoxicity is causing the visual symptoms
distractors.why: Ototoxicity affects hearing and follows rapid IV or high doses.

distractors.text: Digoxin has caused the low potassium by wasting it
distractors.why: The diuretic is the cause of the potassium loss.

why_correct: Loops cause hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia. Hypokalemia increases digoxin toxicity, so potassium, magnesium and creatinine are monitored.
takeaway: Loop + digoxin: watch potassium.
discriminator: The diuretic sets up the toxicity; digoxin delivers it.

stem: A 76-year-old on losartan and spironolactone is treated for a urinary infection with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. Five days later she is weak with peaked T waves. Which mechanism explains this?
correct: Trimethoprim added to two drugs that already raise potassium

distractors.text: Sulfamethoxazole displaced losartan and dropped her pressure
distractors.why: The finding is hyperkalemia, not hypotension.

distractors.text: Trimethoprim induced the metabolism of spironolactone
distractors.why: Lower spironolactone effect would lower potassium.

distractors.text: The antibiotic caused hypokalemia through diarrhea
distractors.why: Peaked T waves point to high potassium.

distractors.text: Losartan caused bradykinin build-up and angioedema
distractors.why: ARBs avoid the bradykinin effect, and this is not angioedema.

why_correct: Potassium supplements and trimethoprim cause hyperkalemia with potassium-sparing diuretics, and with ACE inhibitors and ARBs. Three potassium-raising drugs together is the setup.
takeaway: Trimethoprim counts as a potassium-raising drug.
discriminator: Count the potassium raisers before adding one.
